sections.heading: Standard Testing Procedure for Infusion Pump – ITC India
paragraphs: Ensure accuracy, safety, and compliance of your infusion pumps with NABL-accredited testing and calibration services by ITC India – India’s leading biomedical equipment testing partner.

sections.heading: 🔬 Why Is Infusion Pump Testing Crucial?
paragraphs: Infusion pumps are vital for delivering precise medication doses. A malfunction or inaccurate flow can cause under- or over-infusion, leading to serious clinical risks. Regular testing and calibration ensure that your devices:
💡 Did you know? According to the FDA, infusion pump errors have caused over 56,000 adverse event reports in a single decade. Regular testing significantly reduces this risk.
bullets: Comply with NABL and ISO 17025 guidelines

sections.heading: 🧪 Case Study: Ensuring Accuracy in a Multispecialty Hospital, Mumbai
paragraphs: Client: A NABH-accredited hospital with over 300 beds in Mumbai Device Type: Volumetric and syringe infusion pumps (20 units from brands like B. Braun, Fresenius, and Baxter) Issue: Reports of inconsistent flow rates and unresponsive alarms in two pumps

sections.heading: 🔍 Testing Approach by ITC India
paragraphs: Outcome: All pumps passed post-calibration tests. The hospital improved medication delivery safety and passed NABH audit successfully.

rows: Checked external damages, occlusion points, tubing compatibility, and battery status
Used a calibrated infusion device analyzer (Fluke IDA-5) for flow rate, volume, occlusion pressure
Calibrated 4 devices found outside ±5% flow rate margin
Re-tested for compliance with IEC 60601-2-24 and prepared NABL-traceable certificates

sections.heading: 1: “Infusion Pump Testing Setup”
paragraphs: An engineer in a white lab coat connects a syringe pump to the Fluke IDA-5 analyzer. A digital display shows flow rate in real-time. Calibrated weights and certified test fluids sit on the bench.

sections.heading: 2: “Occlusion Test Simulation”
paragraphs: A technician simulates a blockage in the IV line while monitoring occlusion pressure alerts. The device is tested for auto shutoff and alarm sound within 10 seconds.

sections.heading: 🛠️ Step-by-Step Infusion Pump Testing Procedure
paragraphs: At ITC India, we follow a scientific, traceable, and manufacturer-compliant testing protocol. Here’s a breakdown of our standard operating procedure:

sections.heading: 🔹 1. Pre-Testing Inspection
bullets: Verify pump model, serial number, and test due date.
Check physical condition (casing, connectors, display, keypad).
Ensure the correct infusion set and tubing are used.

sections.heading: 🔹 3. Functional Testing
paragraphs: We simulate real clinical conditions using high-precision analyzers like Fluke IDA-5 or Rigel Multi-Flo to test:
bullets: Flow Rate Accuracy: Verify delivery rate at set points (e.g., 1 mL/h, 5 mL/h, 25 mL/h)
Volume Accuracy: Confirm the total volume delivered matches the programmed value.
Occlusion Pressure: Test device response to line blockage and alarm activation.
Bolus and KVO (Keep Vein Open) modes where applicable.

sections.heading: 🔹 4. Alarm Verification
paragraphs: We simulate different error conditions to confirm alarm function:

sections.heading: 🔹 5. Battery Backup Testing
bullets: Evaluate performance under simulated power failure

sections.heading: 🔹 6. Calibration Adjustment (if required)
paragraphs: If the pump deviates beyond acceptable limits (typically ±5% for flow rate), our experts perform internal calibration following OEM protocols and verify post-adjustment accuracy.

sections.heading: 🔹 7. Documentation & Compliance
bullets: Include test data, calibration due date, and remarks
Compliant with IEC 60601-2-24, ISO 13485, NABL, and hospital audit requirements
